paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.
model_annotation: This bar chart, titled "QAdapter," illustrates the computational cost in terms of floating point operations (FLOPs) for several fine-tuning methods applied to a language model. The horizontal axis displays categorical labels for five methods arranged from left to right: "Full FT," "TAG," "Adapter," "MTL-FT," "QAdapter," and "Ours." The vertical axis is labeled "# FLOPs" and uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^18 to 10^20, with gridlines at each order of magnitude. Each method is represented by a single vertical bar; the first five bars are colored orange, while the final bar labeled "Ours" is colored dark green and its label appears in bold text, visually distinguishing it from the other methods. The tallest bar corresponds to "Full FT," reaching approximately 6 × 10^19 FLOPs. The "TAG" and "Adapter" bars are similar in height, both near approximately 2 × 10^19 FLOPs, with "TAG" being slightly taller. The "MTL-FT" bar is notably shorter, at roughly 3 × 10^18 FLOPs. The "QAdapter" bar is shorter still, at approximately 1.5 × 10^18 FLOPs, and the "Ours" bar is comparable in height to "QAdapter," reaching approximately 1.7 × 10^18 FLOPs. The bars appear to be arranged in a roughly descending order of FLOPs from left to right, with "QAdapter" and "Ours" being the shortest and closest in value.
